reading.body:
Microsoft owns PHX-13, a data center campus in Goodyear, Arizona on West Broadway Road, part of the Phoenix metropolitan area's AI infrastructure footprint. The operator purchased an additional 100 acres adjacent to the existing campus to expand capacity, but Microsoft publishes no individual campus power consumption, square footage, or building-level capacity figures anywhere in its public disclosures. This disclosure policy means the campus's actual load is not known.

The Goodyear campus sits in Arizona, where 56 facilities are mapped but only 4 publish power consumption data. Arizona's published capacity across those four facilities totals 512 MW. Without individual campus figures, PHX-13 cannot be ranked definitively by load, though it is substantial enough to rank fifth among Arizona facilities where power is disclosed at all. Vantage Data Centers operates a separate unrelated campus in the same area under different ownership.

The scale of Microsoft's aggregate infrastructure—80 regions, 500+ datacenters worldwide, 40+ gigawatts of contracted renewable energy—establishes that the company is a top-tier consumer of compute resources. PHX-13's expansion, confirmed as recently as 2026, signals continued investment in the Phoenix region. Without published specifications for this campus, its contribution to Arizona's capacity and grid constraints remains opaque to outside analysis.
